chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one whom this [time] overtakes, and he has thereby attained Hajj. He said: If he arrives at Jam' while the people are at al-Mash'ar al-Haram before the sunrise, he has attained Hajj and his Umrah is not valid. If he attains Jam' after the sunrise, it is a separate Umrah and he has no Hajj. If he wishes to stay in Mecca, he stays; and if he wishes to return to his family, he returns, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَام: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the specific spot at Muzdalifah where standing is required
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam' (Muzdalifah), the place where pilgrims gather after leaving Mina
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَة: Umrah Munfradah, a standalone pilgrimage distinct from Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses the Muzdalifah stay until after sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the critical distinction between Hajj and Umrah based on the timing of the stay at Muzdalifah (Jam' al-Mash'ar al-Haram) relative to sunrise. It establishes that arriving before sunrise validates the Hajj, while arriving after sunrise invalidates it, reducing the ritual to a standalone Umrah and making Hajj obligatory for the following year. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of ritual pillars as a condition for the validity of the pilgrimage.
